entities.summary: Willem Barentsz, anglicized as William Barents or Barentz, was a Dutch navigator, cartographer, and Arctic explorer. Born in 1550, Barents was the son of a Protestant pastor and received a classical education. He began his maritime career at 16, working on various Dutch merchant ships before joining the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in 1590. Barents's most significant achievement was his two voyages to the Arctic in 1594-1597, which led to the discovery of the northern coast of Siberia, the island of Novaya Zemlya, and the New Siberian Islands. This expedition, commissioned by the VOC, made Barents the first European to navigate the Arctic Ocean. Barents's maps of the Arctic region, which were highly accurate and detailed, were instrumental in the development of Dutch maritime trade in the region. He died on June 20, 1597, at the age of 47, during a return voyage to the Netherlands. Barents's legacy extends beyond his explorations, as his work helped to establish the Dutch as a major maritime power in the region. His maps and writings also contributed to a greater understanding of the Arctic environment and its indigenous peoples.
